orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL 
Second Appeal No. 110 of 2013
with
Stay Application No. 8767 of 2013
1. Lakhi Ram Joshi
S/o Late Shri Mani Ram Joshi
R/o 28, South Vanasthali Mandir Lane,
Ballupur, Dehradun 
…................Appellant 
Versus
1. Smt. Malti Devi 
D/o Fakir Chand 
W/o Shri Bhagwat Hari 
R/o Village Ballupur Mauja Garhi, 
Pargana Kendriya Doon District Dehradun
2. Jagdish Narayan
S/o Shri Raja Ram 
R/o Ballupur Mauja Garhi, 
Pargana Kendriya Doon District Dehradun
3. Smt. Savetri @ Leela Devi
W/o Radha Krishna
R/o Ballupur Mauja Garhi, 
Pargana Kendriya Doon District Dehradun
4. Shri Baboo Ram
S/o Radha Krishna
R/o Ballupur Mauja Garhi, 
Pargana Kendriya Doon District Dehradun 
5. Smt. Sanoo Devi
W/o Baboo Ram 
R/o Ballupur Mauja Garhi, 
Pargana Kendriya Doon District Dehradun
 
……..Defendants/Performa Respondents 2
Shri Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate, assisted by Shri D.C.S.
Rawat, Advocate, present for the defendant/appellant. 
Hon’ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
Heard.
(2) This second appeal is directed against the judgment
and decree dated 08.07.2013, passed by Vth Additional
District Judge, Dehradun, in Civil Appeal No. 70 of 2011
whereby said court has partly allowed the appeal. 
(3) Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that a
suit for cancellation of sale deed and declaration and
injunction was dismissed by the trial court, but the lower
appellate court without disturbing the findings recorded by
the trial court has passed a perpetual injunction directing
the defendants not to evict her from the room occupied by
her without due process of law. 
(4) Admit the second appeal on following substantial
question of law:-
Whether the lower appellate court has erred in law in
not appreciating that Shri Dome S/o Gayadeen had no
authority to execute a Will on 14.05.1971, in favour of the
plaintiff after Shri Dome had already executed registered
sale deed on 27.11.1968 in favour of Rajendra Singh 3
(predecessor in title of defendant) ?
(5) Issue notice to respondents.
(6) Summon the lower court record.
(7) Having heard learned counsel for the appellant, and
after going through the impugned judgment and decree
passed by the lower appellate court, as an interim measure,
it is directed that respondent No.1 shall not change the
nature of the property until further orders of this court.
(Stay Application No. 8767 of 2013 stands disposed of).
(8) List after service of notice on the respondents. 
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt.23.08.2013
N.P

SA 110/2013
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Sr. 
Advocate, assisted by Mr. G.D. Joshi, 
Advocate for the defendant/appellant. 
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Sr. Advocate, 
assisted by Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for 
the respondent no. 1/plaintiff. 
Having heard learned Sr. 
Counsels for the parties, it transpires 
that the defendant/appellant purchased 
a property on 14.3.2002 from the true 
owner vide a sale deed. Respondent no. 
1/plaintiff Smt. Malti Devi was 
admittedly in possession of one room of 
such property. She instituted a suit for 
cancellation of the sale deed. The said 
suit was dismissed. First appeal also 
failed, but a direction was made therein 
that Smt. Malti Devi shall not be evicted 
from the room, which is under her 
occupation. This part of the judgment 
has been challenged by the 
appellant/defendant Lakhi Ram Joshi. 
Now, a miscellaneous application 
(CLMA 1705/2016) has been moved 
seeking ad interim injunction order 
against the respondent no. 1/plaintiff not 
to interfere in possession of the appellant 
over the property except the room in 
which the respondent no. 1/plaintiff was 
found in possession by the lower 
appellate court. This application has been 
opposed by learned Sr. Counsel of the 
plaintiff/respondent no. 1 on the premise 
that under the garb of the orders of first 
appellate court, Smt. Malti Devi is being 
resisted by the appellant/defendant from 
using even the land and the passage 
appurtenant to such room. 
Learned Sr. Counsel prays for 
and is granted two weeks’ time to file  objections against the said miscellaneous 
application. Along with the objections, 
the respondent no. 1/plaintiff shall also 
file the photographs, taken from all 
dimensions, of the room under her 
occupation. 
List after two weeks. 
Meanwhile, status quo shall be 
maintained by both the parties. 
Let the certified copy of this order 
be supplied to learned Counsel for 
respondent no. 1 today itself on his 
expenses. 
 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
 3.3.2016 
Prabodh

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Sharma,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Alok Singh,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari
orders.text:
SA No. 110 of 2013
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Sr.
Advocate assisted by Mr. Devang Dobhal,
Advocate for the appellant. 
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Sr. Advocate
assisted by Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate for
the respondents.
Having heard the learned Senior
Counsels for the parties, it transpires
that at the time of admission of this
second appeal on 23.08.2013, ad interim
injunction was passed to maintain the
status-quo at the spot and parties were
directed not to change the nature of the
property.
Miscellaneous application (CLMA
1705/2016) moved by the defendant￾appellant on 1st March, 2016 seeking
further an injunction directing the
respondent no.1/plaintiff not to interfere
in his peaceful possession over the
property except the room, in which,
respondent no.1 was found in possession
by the Lower Appellate Court and
direction was issued to the appellant not
to evict the respondent no.1 from the said
room except in accordance with law. 
Having received the copy of this
added injunction application, cross￾objections (CLMA 2245/2016) were filed
on 14th March, 2016 under Order 41 Rule
22 CPC by the respondent no.1/plaintiff
with the delay condonation application
(CLMA 2242/2016) seeking to condone
the delay of 879 days. 
Plaintiff-respondent no.1 has filed
several photographs of the spot, which
suggest that she is in occupation of the land, in controversy, by means of a large
tin shed structure, which is more than 
one and all these tin shades would
certainly have the Kitchen, Wash
Room/Toilets, without them, comfortable
living of any family is not possible. The
photographs also suggest that this old
lady Smt. Malti Devi has grown up
daughters/children, who are living in this
tin shed structure. 
So, mentioning of “dwelling room”
in the operative portion of the Appellate
Court’s judgment, prima facie, it appears
not confined to small single room,
therefore, delay, which has caused in
filing the cross-objections, seems to be on
account of filing fresh application (CLMA
1705/2016) by the defendant-appellant,
is condonable, so, I condone the delay of
879 days. Delay condonation application
(CLMA 2242/2016) is accordingly allowed
and cross-objections are taken on record
and the same shall be finally adjudicated
at the time of final hearing of this second
appeal. 
LCR has been received. 
List in the second week of
November, 2016 for final hearing. 
 
 
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 24.10.2016
Nadim
